title: Cycle detection & weighted adjacency lists
overview: This module asks: does a graph contain a cycle? In an undirected graph a visited neighbour that is not your parent means a cycle; in a directed graph you need to know whether the neighbour is still on the current DFS path. It also shows how to store edge weights, preparing for Dijkstra.

concepts.explain: While exploring `u`, if a neighbour `v` is already visited and `v` is not `u`'s parent, there is another way to reach `v`, so a cycle exists.
Record `parent[child] = u` when discovering a child (or pass `parent` as a DFS argument).
Keep `pathvisit[]`: true while a node is on the current recursion path. Reaching a node that is still on the path means a back edge, a cycle.

concepts.term: Why the undirected rule fails for directed graphs
concepts.explain: In a directed graph two arrows can meet at the same node (0→2, 1→2) without any cycle, so "already visited" is not enough.
Start a search from every unvisited node so no piece is skipped.

files.title: Adjacency list with weights
files.what: Reads `a b c` edges and stores `{b, c}` in `a`'s list and `{a, c}` in `b`'s list, then prints them.
steps: `vector<pair<int,int>> adj_list[n]`.
For each edge push `{b, c}` to `a` and `{a, c}` to `b`.
Print each node's neighbours as `node (weight)`.
files.complexity: Time O(n + e) · Space O(n + e)
files.input_note: `n e`, then e lines `a b weight`.
files.output_note: `0 -> 1 (5)2 (3)` means node 0 connects to 1 with cost 5 and to 2 with cost 3 (there is no space between items, so read carefully).
files.watch_out: Add a space after `)` in the print for easier reading.

check.q: What does `p.second` hold in this list?

files.title: Undirected cycle detection (BFS)
files.what: BFS from every unvisited node; a visited neighbour that is not the current node's parent means a cycle.
steps: Set `parent` to -1 and `cycle = false`.
In BFS, for each `child` of `par`: if `vis[child]` and `parent[par] != child`, set `cycle = true`.
Unvisited children are pushed with `parent[child] = par`.
Loop over all nodes to cover every component, then print the result.
files.input_note: 5 nodes: triangle 0-1-2 plus a separate edge 3-4.
files.watch_out: Tip: on some compilers you need `#include <cstring>` for `memset`; this file relies on another header bringing it in.

check.q: Why is seeing your own parent again not a cycle?
check.a: In an undirected graph the edge back to your parent is the same edge you came through.

files.title: Undirected cycle detection (DFS)
files.what: Same parent rule written with recursive DFS.
steps: `dfs(src)` marks `src`.
For each `child`: visited and not `parent[src]` → cycle.
Unvisited child: set `parent[child] = src` and recurse.
files.input_note: A simple path 0-1-2-3-4 (a tree, so no cycle).
files.output_note: Prints `No Cycle`: the edges form a simple path 0-1-2-3-4.
files.watch_out: Tip: on some compilers you need `#include <cstring>` for `memset`; this file relies on another header bringing it in.

check.q: A connected undirected graph has V nodes and V edges. Must it have a cycle?
check.a: Yes. A tree has exactly V-1 edges; one more always makes a cycle.

files.title: Directed cycle detection (DFS + path array)
files.what: Uses `pathvisit` to know which nodes are on the current DFS path; an edge to such a node closes a cycle.
steps: On entering `src`: `vis[src] = pathvisit[src] = true`.
For each child: if it is visited **and** on the path, set `cycle = true`.
If it is not visited, recurse.
On leaving `src`: `pathvisit[src] = false`.
files.output_note: Prints `Cycle Detected`: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 1 loops back to a node still on the path.
files.watch_out: Tip: on some compilers you need `#include <cstring>` for `memset`; this file relies on another header bringing it in.

check.q: Why must `pathvisit[src]` be reset to false when DFS leaves `src`?
check.a: Once we back out, `src` is no longer on the current path; a later arrow into it is not a cycle.

files.title: GFG - Detect cycle in an undirected graph (DFS)

problem.name: GFG - Detect cycle in an undirected graph

files.what: Returns true as soon as the DFS finds a visited neighbour that is not its parent; `parent` is passed as an argument.
steps: `isCycle` loops over all nodes and starts `dfs(i, -1, ...)` on unvisited ones.
`dfs` marks `src`; a visited `child != parent` returns true.
An unvisited child is explored with `dfs(child, src, ...)`; a true result is passed up at once.
files.input_note: Driver format: number of cases; each is `V E` then E edges. A triangle, then a simple path.
files.output_note: `isCycle = true` for the triangle and `isCycle = false` for the path.

check.q: What is the benefit of passing `parent` as a parameter instead of a global array?
check.a: Each call carries its own parent, so no extra array is needed and the code is self-contained.

files.title: CSES 1192 - Counting Rooms
files.what: Counts connected floor areas with DFS on the grid.
steps: Read the map.
For each unvisited `.` cell: `dfs` and `cnt++`.
`dfs` spreads over valid, unvisited `.` cells.
files.input_note: The sample building from the task.
files.output_note: Prints `3`: the two small rooms on the left and the big room on the right.
files.watch_out: On a 1000x1000 open map the recursion can go 10^6 calls deep. That is fine with a big judge stack but would crash on a default 1 MB stack; BFS avoids the risk. Tip: on some compilers you need `#include <cstring>` for `memset`; this file relies on another header bringing it in.

practice_links.name: Detect cycle in an undirected graph
Maximum Number of Fish in a Grid

recap: Undirected cycle: visited neighbour that is not the parent.
Directed cycle: neighbour still on the current DFS path (`pathvisit`).
Always loop over all nodes for disconnected graphs.

check_yourself.q: Directed edges 0→1, 0→2, 1→2. Is there a cycle?
check_yourself.a: No. Node 2 is reached twice, but it is not on the path when reached the second time.

check_yourself.q: Why can BFS detect undirected cycles but is awkward for directed ones?
check_yourself.a: BFS has no notion of the current path, which the directed rule needs.

check_yourself.q: What changes in the adjacency list for a directed weighted graph?
check_yourself.a: Push only `{b, w}` into `adj[a]`, not the reverse.
